chunks: And Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Ali ibn al-Nu'man from Abu al-Subbah from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding the Mukatab:

He pays part of his manumission debt, then dies, leaving a son and wealth greater than what he owes in manumission. He said: He pays his masters the remainder of the manumission debt, and what remains is for his son.

key_terms.المُكَاتَبِ: A slave who has entered into a contract to pay a specific sum to his master for his freedom
key_terms.مُكَاتَبَتِهِ: The manumission debt or contract price

ai.seo_question: How is the estate of a Mukatab distributed if he dies with a remaining manumission debt and a surviving son?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Isfarayini clarifies the distribution of a Mukatab's estate, prioritizing the settlement of the remaining manumission debt with the masters before the surplus passes to the heir, specifically the son. It highlights the Shia juristic view that the Mukatab's freedom is contingent upon full payment, ensuring creditors (masters) are satisfied before inheritance distribution. This ruling underscores the legal status of the Mukatab as a free person in terms of inheritance rights, distinct from a fully enslaved individual.
